projects.name: SDG budget tagging and coding of the national budget
projects.description: The realization of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) remains a challenge for Sri Lanka despite having made significant strides in reducing poverty and promoting social development over the last decades. Currently, Sri Lanka faces a period of adjustment as it addresses a challenging socio-economic context exacerbated due to the COVID-19 pandemic. ‘Better budgeting’ in the context of 2030 Agenda means explicit and measurable presentation of SDG targets in budget allocations and reports (and in other elements of the budget cycle) and use of those in budget decision-making. When SDGs become part of the country’s national policy framework, it is crucial that the process is then followed by SDG integration into the countries’ budgetary frameworks.  If not integrated into the budgets, then it is very likely to expect disconnects between the strategic planning frameworks that have made commitments to the 2030 Agenda on the one hand, and public budgets that remain driven by “business as usual” on the other. UNDP has recruited a consultant to engage in an SDG Budget Tagging exercise as requested by the Government of Sri Lanka. This exercise is being conducted in partnership with the Sri Lanka Sustainable Development Council and the National Budget Department of the Ministry of Finance. This assignment is expected to support policy-based and standardized codification system to identify, tag, and monitor SDG initiatives across government agencies through the National Budget, thereby strengthening the country's SDG planning, implementation, and financing capabilities

projects.description: Sri Lanka does not have a formal INFF progamme underway, although many of the building blocks are being put in place and it is effectively formulating the INFF bottom up. Government’s proposed fiscal strategy in the medium term (2022-25) and macroeconomic direction (MoF Annual Report 2021, p.9) encompasses a focus on increasing the allocation of funds and enhancing targeting of such funds for the most vulnerable segments of the society to uplift their livelihoods under the social safety net programme. Both UNICEF and UNDP are focusing on these issues in the context of the current economic crisis. The focus here is on taking forward the INFF building block on social protection, through policy advocacy to make the most effective case for sustainable investment in social protection, including to address the needs of the new poor not covered by existing programmes, and where there is a need to protect and scale and not just support emergency cash transfers.

projects.name: SDG Investor Map-Post Lauch activity
projects.description:
"UNDP Sri Lanka and UNDP’s SDG Impact in partnership with the Sustainable Development Council and Board of Investments for Sri Lanka, launched the Sri Lanka SDG Investor Map on the 30th of August 2022. The map has identified 15 investment opportunity areas across 5 key sectors which include, Healthcare, Renewable Energy, Food and Beverages, Consumer Goods, and Infrastructure. Application of technology, Gender, Education, and climate are cross-cutting themes that were explored for every sector, sub-sector and investment themes. 53% of the business models are seeking funding over USD 1 million, this includes the majority of the IOAs under Renewable Energy, and some of the IOAs related to Healthcare, Food and Beverage and Consumer Goods.  Keeping in mind the challenging economic climate that Sri Lanka is currently experiencing and the importance of directing private investment to the country, the Sri Lanka Country Office has put together the following plan to accelerate private sector capital flows: 

-Investment activation towards SDG enabling IOAs (focusing on sector deep-dive sessions, themed accelerator programmes) 
-Translating white spaces into action (focusing on 1.	Series of round table discussions on white spaces identified in the Investor Map for Sri Lanka, policy briefs) 
-Outreach and communication (includes webinar to introduce the SDG Impact Standards, At least 2 blogs/Op-ed to present map findings) 
-Updating the SDG Investor Map "
